en: Bamboo is actually a type of grass, and some species can grow up to 91 centimeters in just one single day.
The peacock mantis shrimp punches so fast that it boils the surrounding water, creating a flash of light and heat rivaling the sun's surface.
Your stomach produces a brand-new protective mucus lining every two weeks to prevent its strong acids from digesting its own tissue.
A single mature dandelion plant can produce over 15,000 seeds in one year, and each seed has its own tiny parachute for wind dispersal.
The bare-nosed wombat produces cube-shaped feces to stop the droppings from rolling away, helping them mark their territory on rocks and logs.
If uncoiled, all the DNA in your body would stretch from Earth to the Sun and back over a dozen times.
The Venus flytrap counts electrical signals from a trapped insect's legs to ensure it only closes its leaves on live, moving prey.
The archerfish shoots jets of water from its mouth to knock insects off overhanging branches, accurately calculating the light refraction of the water.
During metamorphosis, a caterpillar completely digests itself inside its chrysalis into a nutrient-rich soup before rebuilding its body into an adult butterfly.
Babies are born with about 300 soft bones, but many fuse together as they grow, leaving adults with exactly 206 solid bones.
Trees in a forest share nutrients and send distress signals through an underground network of fungal threads called the wood wide web.
Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of space by curling into a dehydrated ball called a tun and completely pausing their metabolism.
